authTierRationale: Two credential modes are offered and the easiest is a single self-serve Personal Access Token that the user generates in the Asana developer console and pastes into `credentials.personal_access_token`; it is sent as a bearer token with no app registration (source.py returns airbyte_cdk TokenAuthenticator for it). The OAuth mode is standalone T3_BYO_REFRESH — spec.json requires client_id, client_secret AND refresh_token, and the connector only ever performs a refresh_token grant against https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token (it never runs the authorization_code leg itself). Estuary's hosted control plane supplies the app: __main__.py declares flow.OAuth2Spec(provider='asana') with the authorize/token URL templates and spec.json declares advanced_auth with complete_oauth_server_input/output specs, so on the hosted platform the user only clicks through consent. That hosted convenience does not change the standalone tier, and it is moot for the overall rating because the PAT path is already T1.

unionMisfits.description: pathPlaceholders is typed as a map for parent-scoped PATHS, but roughly half of Asana's parent scoping is applied as a QUERY PARAM instead of a path segment (projects/tags/users take `workspace=`, tasks takes `project=`, attachments_compact and events take `parent=`/`resource=`, portfolios_memberships takes `portfolio=`). Modelling those as pathPlaceholders is a lie about where the value goes; modelling them only in `params` loses the fact that they come from iterating a parent stream. I recorded both (the value appears in `params` and the provenance in `pathPlaceholders`) and disambiguated in the description text, but the schema should say this explicitly.

attachments_compact and events each concatenate TWO independent parent slice generators (projects gids AND tasks gids) into the same placeholder. A single-valued map cannot express 'this placeholder is fed by the union of two parent streams'.

attachments, sections, stories, portfolios and organization_exports are not collection endpoints at all: they issue ONE GET per id harvested from a companion `*_compact` stream and return a single object under /data, not an array. There is no page to paginate. The PullSpec union has no way to say 'record-detail fan-out' as distinct from 'list endpoint', so a reader cannot tell that stories costs one request per story (the full chain is workspaces -> projects -> tasks -> stories_compact -> stories, i.e. potentially millions of requests; the connector itself caps this at 100 slices under test_mode because tests exceeded two hours).

Every request carries an `opt_fields` query param whose value is COMPUTED at runtime from the stream's own JSON schema (top-level scalars verbatim, nested objects as `<prop>.gid`, with per-stream overrides in Tasks/Users/Stories). params is typed as a static map, so the single most important query parameter in this connector cannot be represented faithfully — omitting it would make Asana return only gid/name/resource_type and silently truncate every column.

opt_fields.rule: scalars verbatim; object props as <prop>.gid; per-stream overrides

unionMisfits.description: The Asana events endpoint is a sync-token change feed, not a list: `sync` is both the pagination token and the resume token, and a 412 means the token expired and the caller must re-snapshot. That is execution.continuity-shaped (our-side loss on a stale token) but execution.mode is 'poll' and the schema only requires continuity for mode 'log'. Worse, the connector holds sync_token on the instance and never persists it across runs, and never seeds it, so in practice this behaves as a full re-read.

continuity.ourSideLoss: sync token invalidated -> HTTP 412 -> full re-read

unionMisfits.description: Neither the connector nor the estuary-cdk Airbyte shim declares any interval or cron. The only scheduling knob found is `intervalSeconds` on the platform-side CaptureSpec in estuary_cdk/flow.py, which the connector never sets. There is no connector-owned schedule to record.

Likely BUG worth flagging rather than modelling: OrganizationExports.stream_slices yields a list containing a single DICT COMPREHENSION (`yield from [{'organization_export_gid': id for id in self._organization_export_ids}]`) rather than a list comprehension of dicts, so all keys collapse and only the LAST configured export id is ever fetched. I recorded the intended semantics (one slice per configured id) and note the discrepancy here.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Neither source-asana nor estuary-cdk's Airbyte shim declares an interval or cron. The only scheduling field in scope is `intervalSeconds` on the platform-side CaptureSpec (estuary-cdk/estuary_cdk/flow.py:56), which the connector never sets, so there is no connector-owned default to report.
abstained.streams[*].schedules: Same reason as execution.defaultSchedule: ResourceConfig in shim_airbyte_cdk.py carries only stream / syncMode / namespace / cursorField. No per-binding schedule exists.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is 'poll' and no server-side artifact is created: every stream is a plain GET, and the only stateful token (the Events `sync` token) lives on an in-process attribute that is never persisted to connector state, so nothing accrues on the customer side and nothing is lost by pausing. Reported as null rather than inventing an artifact list. The Events 412 sync-token-expiry path is described under unionMisfits instead.
abstained.streams[*].cursorField: No stream sets default_cursor_field and none registers an incremental sync mode; the shim leaves ResourceConfig.cursor_field at None (confirmed absent from every binding in the discover snapshot). There is no incremental leg, hence incrementalParam is null everywhere.
abstained.streams[*].pull.backfill / streams[*].pu: All 18 discovered bindings report syncMode full_refresh, so there is no historical/ongoing split — the whole collection is re-read each run and the single pull shape is recorded under `snapshot`.
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition: Recorded as 'merge' on the basis that each binding is keyed (/gid, or /created_at for events) and the connector emits no deletions or tombstones, so a repeat full read upserts by key. The connector code itself never states a write disposition, and Estuary's reduction behaviour for a full_refresh binding with a source-defined key is decided outside the connector, so this is a low-confidence inference rather than an extracted fact.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No connector-wide default headers are set on the HttpStream subclasses. The only explicit header construction is the ad-hoc `users/me` lookup, which sends Accept: application/json plus the authenticator's header (streams.py:136-137); whether the paged requests also carry Accept is decided by airbyte_cdk internals that are not vendored here.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.type: source.py passes the token to airbyte_cdk's TokenAuthenticator without arguments; the resulting header name and 'Bearer' prefix come from airbyte_cdk, which is not vendored in this directory (estuary-cdk only shims the Airbyte source interface). Recorded as bearer on the strength of TokenAuthenticator's documented default, not on a line of source read here.
abstained.streams[13,8,11,15,18].pull.snapshot.pag: These detail-fetch streams inherit AsanaStream.next_page_token unchanged, so the offset-cursor paginator is what the code will execute; in practice a single-object /data response carries no next_page and the loop terminates after one request. The recorded paginator is the inherited mechanism, not evidence that these endpoints page.
abstained.streams[17].pull.snapshot.paginator.curs: Events assigns self.sync_token from payload['sync'] inside parse_response, and next_page_token re-reads the body but uses the instance attribute (the in-line assignment there is commented out, streams.py:273). The token therefore comes from the response body key `sync`, but the read is order-dependent between parse_response and next_page_token; classified cursor/tokenFrom=body with medium confidence.
abstained.streams[18].pull.snapshot: organization_exports never appears in the discover snapshot because it is only registered when the undeclared config field organization_export_ids is present. Its path and slice source are read from code; the primaryKey /gid is inferred from AsanaStream's class default (primary_key = 'gid'), not confirmed by a snapshot.
